newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee surges on chart-driven spec buying.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee surges on chart-driven spec buying.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures finished sharply higher Wednesday, with the May contract jumping some six percent, on chart-driven speculative buying amid a background of continued supply concerns, dealers said.
May settled up 10.95 cents at 189.70 cents a lb after trading from 190.00 to 177.10. Second-month July settled 8.65 cents higher at 173.15 cents, while the back months closed up 6.00 to down 0.75.
Coffee prices headed lower at the outset, but local shortcovering emerged after the May contract managed to hold above chart supprt at 175.00 cents, traders said.
Upward momentum accelerated after May rose through the 180.00-cent level, touching off commission house buy-stops around 183.00, then 185.00 cents.
"The market has been coiling up to do something," said Smith Barney analyst Walt Spilka. "It ran into buy orders and ratcheted up, but not because of any new fundamental development."
Strength in the nearby May/July switch, which widened to 16.55 cents from 14.25 at the close Tuesday, also bolstered the market, traders said.
Additionally, they said a lack of selling by origins who are reportedly well sold contributed to today's exaggerated upswing.
"Producers normally get most of their coffee out in the first quarter," one trader said. "And they are not going to aggressively sell what they have left ahead of the (Brazil) frost season."
Traders noted the decline in total open interest to 33,038 lots as of April 8, from more than 40,000 lots a month ago, increased volatility -- which also distorted price moves.

Technically, traders said a chart gap above the market in May between 190.50 and 192.00 will likely be filled on Thursday. But they added the 200.00 level would pose strong resistance. Support was seen around 185.00, then 183.00.
On the fundamental side, Smith Barney's Spilka said recent dips in coffee stocks certified for delivery against the exchanged served to remind people of the near-term supply tightness.
"The stocks at the exchange are going lower again," Spilka said. "And they are probably just going to get tighter."
After Wednesday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks were off 250 60-kg bags, to 81,578 bags as of April 8. There were no bags pending grading, the exchange said.

Some dealers said Brazilian stevedores' continued occupation of vessels at the terminal of steel firm Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) at the key port of Santos may have been viewed as supportive, although there was no word of any delays in coffee shipments.
The stevedores, however, maintained their promise to start a strike at Santos should the steel firm attempt to load or unload any vessels at its terminal.
Additionally, other traders said a strike by Colombian truckers set for April 20 could also heighten supply jitters.
Volume reached an estimated 10,430 lots, up from Tuesday's official tally of 5,499 lots. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk 212 859 1640))
